content.text: {"headline":"Approve R2 (demand cut, breaks moved past the peak, peak overtime for 21 payments agents 13:30-14:30) at ₹4,284, and bring in the duty manager. It is the best available plan but is predicted at only 57.1% against the 80% target for 13:00-15:00.","why":"The surge comes from the UPI switch outage (INC-20261006-6998). upi_payment_failed calls are running at 2.56x normal. Staffing is at plan (42 of 43 agents) and handle time is below forecast, so this is a demand problem, not a staffing one. R2 tackles both sides. It cuts demand with an IVR outage message and 20% chat deflection on both queues. It adds capacity with overtime concentrated on the 13:30-14:30 peak and moves breaks out of the peak to 14:00-15:00. Predicted service level for 13:00-15:00 is 57.1% (payments 50.1%, general 71.0%), with abandons at 10.2%. Doing nothing gives 30.8% and 21.7% abandons. Rest-of-day service level improves to 82.1%. No plan reaches 80%, and R2 has the highest predicted service level of all options. Escalation is flagged under ESC-02 because 57% is below the 70% escalation line. The duty manager should be involved to consider further measures beyond this plan.","trade_offs":["R1 costs ₹360 more (₹4,644) for slightly worse results: 56.6% overall, 10.6% abandons. It spreads overtime over 1.5 h rather than the peak hour.","P3 (₹3,732) is cheaper but reaches only 47.9%, with payments at 41.7% and abandons at 12.0%.","P2 (₹492) and P4 (₹2,880) reach only 39.7% and 38.2%. The no-cost P1 is no better than doing nothing (29.9%).","The general queue holds at 71.0% under R2, versus 56.2% with no action. It depends on chat deflection and on breaks moving to 14:00-15:00."],"watch":"Track uptake of the 21 overtime offers before 13:30 and whether payments service level is recovering in the 13:30-14:30 intervals. Watch for general-queue service level slipping when the delayed breaks land at 14:00-15:00. Follow INC-20261006-6998 for resolution, which would end the excess upi_payment_failed demand."}
